record.original_question: Is it true that for all but o(2n ) polynomials P (z) min |P (z)| < 1, |z|=1 or, if not, what is the corresponding correct result?

evidence.quote: Is it true that for all but o(2n ) polynomials P (z) min |P (z)| < 1, |z|=1 or, if not, what is the corresponding correct result?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each positive integer $n$, let $\mathcal{P}_n$ denote the set of polynomials of degree at most $n$ with coefficients in $\{+1,-1\}$ (so $|\mathcal{P}_n|=2^{n+1}$). For $P\in\mathcal{P}_n$, define
$$m(P)=\min_{|z|=1}|P(z)|.$$
Let $E_n=\{P\in\mathcal{P}_n : m(P)\ge 1\}$. Determine whether
$$|E_n|=o(2^n)\qquad\text{as }n\to\infty,$$
i.e.\ whether for all but $o(2^n)$ of the $\pm 1$-coefficient polynomials of degree at most $n$ one has $\min_{|z|=1}|P(z)|<1$. If this assertion fails, find the correct asymptotic count of $\{P\in\mathcal{P}_n : m(P)\ge 1\}$ (or, more generally, the correct threshold $c$ such that $\min_{|z|=1}|P(z)|<c$ holds for all but $o(2^n)$ polynomials in $\mathcal{P}_n$).
artifact.category_tag: Littlewood polynomials / minimum modulus on the unit circle
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Cook–Nguyen, "Universality of the minimum modulus for random trigonometric polynomials," Discrete Analysis) establishes universality results for the minimum modulus on the unit circle of random ±1-coefficient polynomials, building on results of Konyagin and Yakir–Zeitouni. However, none of the sources found explicitly state that the specific question — whether $\min_{|z|=1}|P(z)|<1$ holds for all but $o(2^n)$ Littlewood polynomials of degree $n$ — has been resolved in the precise form posed. The exact status of this specific assertion was not verified.

status_evidence.title: Universality of the minimum modulus for random trigonometric polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Extends results about minimum modulus behavior to random ±1 coefficient polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress on the typical minimum modulus of random Littlewood polynomials, but the specific o(2^n) statement is not explicitly addressed.

status_evidence.title: Littlewood polynomial - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Littlewood's problem asks for bounds on values of polynomials with ±1 coefficients on the unit circle.
status_evidence.claim: Littlewood-type problems on the unit circle remain an active area; the precise asymptotic for polynomials with $\min_{|z|=1}|P|\ge 1$ is not standard.
